name: Let Me In makeover show

card.summary: South Korean makeover television programme in which participants receive cosmetic surgery and styling to change their appearance.
card.note: Features surgical procedures; outcomes and risks of surgery apply.

quick.overview:
Let Me In is a South Korean makeover television show in which participants receive cosmetic procedures and styling as a transformation.
It sits within a wider Korean culture of aesthetic surgery; Seoul's Gangnam district is a hub for procedures such as double-eyelid surgery and rhinoplasty.
quick.how: Viewers watch before-and-after transformations; the show itself is not a protocol.
quick.risks: Cosmetic surgery carries standard surgical risks; critics of such shows in Korea have raised concerns about beauty standards.

lead: Let Me In is a South Korean television makeover show featuring cosmetic surgery and styling for its participants.

The show reflects the setting described in coverage of K-beauty: Gangnam is a major hub for aesthetic procedures such as double-eyelid surgery and rhinoplasty, with about 980,000 cosmetic procedures recorded in 2014, roughly half involving South Koreans.[1] The 'Escape the Corset' movement, inspired by #MeToo, pushes back against rigid beauty standards and attitudes toward plastic surgery.[1]

angle.text: Participants receive procedures aimed at changing facial and body appearance; viewers see results and procedure types.

paras: Korean cosmetic surgery is concentrated in Gangnam, with double-eyelid surgery and rhinoplasty common.[1]
